events.text: Port of Seattle officer finds Ridgway parked on a dead-end road near S 192nd St.
King County forms the multi-agency Green River Task Force.
Des Moines police question Ridgway after Marie Malvar’s boyfriend identifies his truck. He denies contact.
Ridgway mails a letter to a newspaper meant to mislead investigators.
Task Force expanded. That spring Ridgway moves the remains of Bush and Sherrill to Tigard, Oregon.
Ridgway contacts the Task Force, is interviewed and passes a polygraph.
A woman reports Ridgway choked her on Pacific Hwy S in 1982. He admits it when questioned.
Search warrant on his home, work locker and vehicles. Saliva sample taken.
Evidence sent to a private lab. No DNA profiles obtainable with existing methods.
Task Force reduced to one investigator, Det. Tom Jensen.
Remains found in 1986 identified as Tracy Winston by mitochondrial DNA.
Jensen submits victims’ evidence to the Washington State Patrol Crime Lab.
WSP lab STR typing matches Ridgway to Chapman, Mills and Christensen.
Arrested in a prostitution sting on Pacific Hwy S and released the same day.
Arrested for murder leaving the Kenworth plant in Renton.
Charged with four counts: Christensen, Hinds, Chapman, Mills.
Prosecutor gives notice of intent to seek the death penalty.
Microtrace finds DuPont Imron paint spheres on Coffield’s and Estes’s clothing.
Three counts added: Coffield, Bonner, Estes.
Plea agreement: cooperation and guilty pleas in exchange for no death penalty.
Ridgway leads investigators to remains of Avent, Buttram and Jane Doe B20.
Marie Malvar’s remains recovered in an Auburn ravine.
Pleads guilty to 48 counts of aggravated first-degree murder.
48 consecutive life terms without parole (Judge Richard A. Jones).
Teenagers find Rebecca Marrero’s skull in an Auburn ravine.
Pleads guilty to the Marrero murder. 49th consecutive life term.
Jane Doe B16 identified as Sandra Major.
Jane Doe B10 identified as Wendy Stephens by genetic genealogy.
Jane Doe B17 identified as Lori Razpotnik by genetic genealogy.
Jane Doe B20 identified as Tammie Liles.
Moved to King County Jail to help search for remains. Returned to Walla Walla Sept 13.
